issues.legal_issue: Property may be requisitioned for a permanent public purpose, although the requisition remains temporary in duration.
material_facts: The proceedings concerned property requisitioned under the state legislation and allotted for residential accommodation or for fair-price ration shops.
The petitioners argued that requisition could not continue to serve the public purposes for which the premises were being used.
issues.conclusion: A permanent public purpose may support an order of requisition; the earlier decision was not to be reconsidered on that basis, and its statement that requisition orders cannot be made for a permanent purpose was not approved.
issues.legal_principle: The words authorising requisition for a public purpose do not restrict the purpose to one that is temporary. Collector of Akola v. Ramchandra held that the purpose may be permanent, and Jiwani Kumar Paraki v. First Land Acquisition Collector supports distinguishing the purpose of requisition from its duration. Requisition differs from acquisition because title remains with the owner; H.D. Vora v. State of Maharashtra remains correct as to the temporary character of requisition, but not as to a bar on permanent purposes.

predicates.requisition_order_case: The matter concerns an order taking possession or control of property for a public purpose without transferring ownership.
predicates.public_purpose_is_permanent: The public purpose for which the property is used is enduring rather than temporary.

issues.definition: When a requisition order serves a public purpose that is enduring, the purpose may still support requisition.

issues.legal_issue: Requisition cannot continue indefinitely or for an unreasonable period, even when it serves a permanent public purpose.
material_facts: Some residential and commercial premises had been requisitioned and occupied for decades, including premises requisitioned more than 45 years earlier.
Many residential premises had been requisitioned in or before 1960, and the requisition orders had not been replaced by acquisition.
The State continued to rely on public needs, including accommodation and the operation of fair-price shops.
issues.conclusion: A requisition order may continue only for a reasonable period in the circumstances of the particular case. Continuation for about 30 years was unreasonable, but 30 years is not a fixed outer limit applicable to every case.
issues.legal_principle: Requisition is temporary in contrast to acquisition, which transfers title. Indefinite or unreasonably prolonged requisition may effectively deprive the owner of the rights of possession and enjoyment without acquisition and due compensation. H.D. Vora v. State of Maharashtra correctly states that requisition cannot continue indefinitely; Jiwani Kumar Paraki v. First Land Acquisition Collector and Mangilal Karwa v. State of M.P. support the distinction between requisition and acquisition. Collector of Akola v. Ramchandra does not conflict because it concerned the permissible nature of the purpose, not indefinite duration. The reasonable period depends on the circumstances, and is ordinarily for the Government to decide.

predicates.requisition_order_continuation_case: The matter concerns whether an existing requisition order may continue.
predicates.continuation_is_indefinite: The requisition is being continued without a meaningful limit on its duration.
predicates.continuation_is_unreasonable_in_case_cir: The duration of the requisition is unreasonable in light of the circumstances of the particular case.

issues.definition: If an existing requisition is indefinite or unreasonable in its circumstances, it must end and the property must be released.

issues.legal_issue: The statutory duty to release requisitioned land also applies to requisitioned premises that are buildings or parts of buildings.
material_facts: The legislation defined land to include buildings and things attached to the earth, while separately defining premises as a building or part of a building let or intended to be let.
The legislation required release of land from requisition by a specified deadline.
The proceedings concerned premises that had been requisitioned.
issues.conclusion: The definition of land includes premises, so the statutory duty to release requisitioned land applies to requisitioned premises as well.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 4(1) and 4(3) define land and premises, respectively, and section 9(1-A) requires release of requisitioned land. The definition of land is broad enough to include a building or part of a building; the separate definition of premises reflects the legislation's former provision for compulsory letting, not an exclusion of premises from the release duty.

predicates.statutory_release_requirement_case: The matter concerns a statutory requirement that requisitioned property be released from requisition.
predicates.requisitioned_property_is_a_building_or_: The property taken under requisition is a building or a part of a building.

issues.definition: When a statutory release requirement applies to requisitioned property that is a building or part of a building, that property is subject to the requirement.

issues.legal_issue: The State is not required by the court to provide alternative accommodation to occupants before releasing requisitioned premises.
material_facts: The occupants sought protection from eviction and relied on the hardship of finding alternative accommodation.
The premises had been requisitioned and the Court required their eventual release.
A separate opinion proposed protective arrangements for certain occupants, but the majority rejected a general requirement to provide alternative accommodation.
issues.conclusion: The State cannot be compelled to provide alternative accommodation to the allottees; whether to provide it is for the State to consider in light of desirability and administrative feasibility. Sawant J. proposed additional protections in a separate opinion.
issues.legal_principle: The majority treated the provision of alternative accommodation as a matter for the State Government's consideration, rather than as a condition that must be satisfied before release of requisitioned premises.

predicates.requisition_release_proceeding: The matter concerns release of property that has been requisitioned.
predicates.occupants_request_alternative_accommodat: The occupants ask the State to provide other accommodation before they leave the requisitioned property.

issues.definition: When occupants request alternative accommodation in a proceeding for release of requisitioned property, the State is not required to provide it.

issues.legal_issue: Occupants whose continued requisition had been quashed were entitled to temporary protection only until the Court's specified transition date, after which they had to vacate.
material_facts: The continued requisition of premises had been quashed in prior proceedings.
Occupants and their legal representatives remained in possession under interim orders of the Court.
The Court considered the difficulty of finding alternative accommodation and directed the State to derequisition the premises and return possession to the landlords.
issues.conclusion: The majority continued the interim protection until the specified date, required the affected occupants to vacate on that date, and directed the State to derequisition the premises and return vacant possession to the landlords by the specified deadline. Sawant J. proposed a longer period of protection for certain groups.
issues.legal_principle: The Court could give transitional protection to occupants affected by orders quashing continued requisition, while preserving the requirement that the State release the property and restore possession to the landlords. The majority's direction was case-specific and did not establish a general maximum period for requisition.

predicates.requisition_order_continuation_case: The matter concerns whether an existing requisition order may continue.
predicates.continued_requisition_has_been_quashed: A court has set aside the continued requisition of the property.
predicates.occupants_remain_under_interim_protectio: The occupants are still in possession under an interim court order.

issues.definition: When continued requisition has been quashed and occupants remain under interim protection, they must vacate after temporary transition.
